model.name: Alias / Same-as Mapping
model.purpose: Provide a reusable, format-neutral mixin for asserting that two or more identifiers or endpoint references denote the same subject, carrying the asserting authority, relation property, confidence, evidence, effective interval and an append-only, idempotent mutation-command surface for changing those assertions.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-036 governs the recorded assertion that identifier endpoints are equivalent (or explicitly not equivalent), including the declared relation property and its binding to a governed vocabulary, directionality and canonical designation, asserting authority and confidence, supporting evidence, effective interval, version chain and lifecycle state. It governs the complete mutation-command surface over those assertions: propose, validate, submit evidence, approve or reject, activate, supersede, retract and quarantine, each requiring an idempotency key and an optimistic-concurrency precondition, each producing immutable append-only records. It does not compute equivalence, does not resolve or merge endpoints, and does not decide or enforce access; those remain with composable sibling models. The model is independent of storage format and access interface: JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections of the same semantics.
in_scope: Equivalence assertions between two or more identifier endpoints, with declared relation property, directionality, canonical designation and explicit not-same (distinctness) constraints.
Asserting authority, confidence declaration, supporting evidence attachments and their provenance.
Effective interval, version chain, lifecycle state and supersession relationships of each assertion.
Mutation-command semantics: propose, validate, submit evidence, approve/reject, activate, supersede, retract and emergency quarantine marking.
Command envelope requirements: idempotency key, canonical request fingerprint, optimistic-concurrency validator and command receipt.

Declarative validation check set (endpoint reference and version, relation-property contract, type/scheme/context compatibility, required evidence and review, contradictions, not-same constraints, effective interval, declared access scope) and machine-readable validation outcome records.
Failure classification, partial-failure detection and compensating-record derivation within this register.
out_of_scope: Entity matching, similarity scoring, blocking and probabilistic record linkage that would produce candidate equivalences.
Reasoning, entailment closure or substitution over asserted equivalences (for example computing owl:sameAs or skos:exactMatch transitive closure).
Identifier resolution, canonical redirect execution, endpoint dereferencing and record merge.
Authorization decisions, policy evaluation and enforcement over commands or over the aliased subjects.
Audit-trail construction, tamper-evident logging and retention scheduling of audit records.
Notification, message delivery and transport-level retry execution.
Minting of new subject identifiers and definition of the subject types themselves, which belong to the parent model.
Physical deletion or erasure of stored records.

boundary_notes.distinction: This model records equivalence that has been asserted by a named authority together with its evidence; it never derives equivalence. Authoritative practice is explicit that an alias assertion is not proof: DID Core states that the presence of an alsoKnownAs assertion does not prove the assertion is true and that a requesting party is strongly advised to obtain independent verification.

SKOS makes skos:exactMatch symmetric and transitive, and OWL 2 gives owl:sameAs full substitution semantics under no unique name assumption. Those entailments are computed by external reasoners over the asserted statements; this model stores only asserted statements, declared bindings and validation outcomes, and never materialises a closure.
This model records which endpoint is designated canonical and which are equivalent; resolution, redirect execution and endpoint merge are performed by the resolver or the owning master system.

A command envelope declares an access scope, and validation checks that the declared scope is registered and not broader than the scope recorded on the target assertion. Whether the actor may act is decided elsewhere; the verifiable-credentials model makes the same separation by stating that verifiability does not imply truth and that relying parties validate against their own policies.

Command receipts, validation reports, decision assertions and transition records are domain state of the alias register. Tamper-evident audit logging, log retention and log query are owned by the referenced audit model; this model emits correlation data only and never writes or reads an audit log.

Idempotency-Key and If-Match/If-Unmodified-Since are transport bindings of model-level preconditions defined here. The model requires an idempotency key and a concurrency validator abstractly; HTTP status codes such as 409, 412 and 422 are projections of model outcome codes, not the semantics themselves.

This model appends tombstones and disposition references and retains superseded records for historic reference, consistent with registry practice that entries are marked deprecated or obsolete rather than deleted. Retention schedules, legal hold and physical erasure are executed by the adopting Dimension's retention and privacy models.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
sources.relevance: Defines idempotent methods (Sec. 9.2.2), conditional-request preconditions If-Match / If-None-Match / If-Unmodified-Since (Sec. 13.1), strong and weak validators and entity-tags (Sec. 8.8.1, 8.8.3), 409 Conflict (Sec. 15.5.10), 412 Precondition Failed (Sec. 15.5.13), 503 and Retry-After (Sec. 15.6.4, 10.2.3). Grounds the optimistic-concurrency precondition and stale-version outcomes.

sources.title: The Idempotency-Key HTTP Header Field (draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header-07)
sources.version_or_date: draft-07, 2025-10-15; expired Internet-Draft, not a standard
sources.relevance: Defines the client-generated idempotency key, key uniqueness and non-reuse across differing payloads, optional server-side request fingerprinting, composite lookup keys, published key-expiry policy, and the duplicate-handling outcomes: cached result on completed replay, conflict while the original is still processing, and rejection when a key is reused with a different payload. Cited as work in progress, not as a normative requirement.

sources.title: RFC 9457: Problem Details for HTTP APIs
sources.relevance: Defines the machine-readable failure document: type, title, status, detail, instance (Sec. 3.1), extension members that consumers must ignore when unrecognised (Sec. 3.2), the guidance to represent the most relevant problem rather than a generic batch type, and the validation-error pattern using an errors extension array with pointers to the offending element.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Mandatory seconds in partial-time and mandatory time-offset of Z or +/-hh:mm (Sec. 5.6); the -00:00 convention for a known UTC instant with unknown local offset (Sec. 4.3); string-sortability conditions for time-ordered sequences (Sec. 5.1). Grounds the timestamp rule and the separation of event, observation and effective times.

sources.title: RFC 8126 (BCP 26): Guidelines for Writing an IANA Considerations Section in RFCs
sources.relevance: Registry governance: registration request contents (Sec. 3.1), registration policies including Expert Review and Specification Required (Sec. 4.5, 4.6), change control and named change controller (Sec. 2.3), modification of existing registrations under the same review as new registrations (Sec. 3.2), and status marking as reserved, deprecated or obsolete with entries retained for historic purposes rather than deleted (Sec. 6, 9.6).

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Supplies the provenance pattern for append-only records: Entity, Activity, Agent; wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom, wasRevisionOf, wasAttributedTo, qualifiedAssociation; generatedAtTime, invalidatedAtTime and wasInvalidatedBy for expressing retraction as invalidation rather than deletion.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference
sources.relevance: Defines the mapping-property vocabulary bound by an alias assertion: exactMatch, closeMatch, broadMatch, narrowMatch, relatedMatch under skos:mappingRelation; symmetry of relatedMatch/closeMatch/exactMatch; transitivity of exactMatch; the disjointness of exactMatch with broadMatch and relatedMatch, which is the normative basis for the contradiction check.

sources.title: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
sources.relevance: Supplies the validation-report structure: ValidationReport with conforms and result; ValidationResult with focusNode, resultPath, value, sourceShape, sourceConstraintComponent, resultMessage and resultSeverity (Violation, Warning, Info); and the separation of data graph from shapes graph, which grounds the check-catalogue / instance-report split.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Primer (Second Edition)
sources.relevance: States that OWL does not make the unique name assumption, that stating two names denote the same individual licenses transfer of all information between them, and that distinctness must be asserted explicitly. Grounds the not-same constraint and the treatment of same/different pairs as a contradiction rather than a merge instruction.

sources.title: Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0
sources.relevance: Supplies the effective-interval pattern (validFrom / validUntil as RFC 3339 date-times), the evidence property describing how an issuer verified claims before issuance, credentialStatus with status checking explicitly defined elsewhere, and the separation between an issuer asserting and a verifier deciding under its own policy.

sources.title: Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) v1.0
sources.relevance: Defines alsoKnownAs as a set of URIs asserting other identifiers for the same subject, states that equivalence should not be assumed unless the relationship is reciprocated, and warns that the presence of an alsoKnownAs assertion does not prove it is true so independent verification is strongly advised. Grounds directionality, reciprocity and the no-inference boundary.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 11179-6:2023 Information technology — Metadata registries (MDR) — Part 6: Registration
sources.relevance: Establishes that registration of an administered item specifies the information to be supplied, the conditions to be met and the procedures to be followed, under a registration authority. Consulted through the ISO catalogue record only; the normative status enumeration was not accessible, so it is used as an alignment for the existence of a governed registration procedure, not as a source of specific status values.

bundles.name: Command Envelope, Concurrency Control and Pre-commit Validation
bundles.description: Everything a mutation command must carry before the alias register will consider it, and everything the register checks before any record is appended: command identity and idempotency, the optimistic-concurrency precondition, the declarative validation check set and the machine-readable outcome or failure report.
bundles.rationale: Alias assertions are federated statements about identity that other systems act on; an unsafe retry, a lost update or an unvalidated contradiction propagates a false equivalence. HTTP semantics supply the normative precondition and conflict vocabulary, the idempotency-key work supplies duplicate-command handling, SHACL supplies the report structure and Problem Details supplies the failure projection. Grouping them as one concern keeps the accept/reject gate in a single auditable place.

layers.name: Command Envelope and Concurrency Control
layers.description: The identity, idempotency and version-precondition contract that every mutation command must satisfy, and how duplicate, in-flight and stale commands are distinguished from one another.

findings.name: Idempotency key, request fingerprint and duplicate-command resolution
findings.description: Every mutation command carries a client-generated idempotency key and is reduced to a canonical fingerprint. The register keeps a receipt series keyed by (submitting client, idempotency key) and uses it to classify an arriving command as a first occurrence, an in-flight duplicate, a completed replay whose recorded outcome is returned unchanged, or a key reuse with a differing payload. This makes retry safe for commands that are not naturally idempotent, without ever applying an effect twice.

questions.text: What command identifier, idempotency key and command-type code must a mutation command carry before the alias register will accept it for processing?
answer_data: Command identifier minted by the submitting agent
Idempotency key value and its generation method (for example a random UUID)
Command-type code drawn from the governed command vocabulary
Submitting client or agent reference forming the composite lookup key

questions.text: Which parts of a command are included in the canonical fingerprint compared against a replayed idempotency key, and which are deliberately excluded?
answer_data: Included: command type, target assertion reference, endpoint references, relation property, effective interval, declared access scope, evidence references
Excluded: transport headers, trace identifiers, observation timestamp, retry counter
Canonicalisation profile identifier and digest algorithm identifier
Fingerprint digest value

questions.text: How is an incoming command classified as a first occurrence, an in-flight duplicate, a completed replay or a key reuse with a different payload?
answer_data: Receipt lookup result for the composite key
Receipt state value (accepted, in-progress, completed, failed)
Fingerprint comparison result (match or mismatch)
Resulting outcome code and, for a completed replay, the reference to the previously recorded outcome

questions.text: How long is a command receipt retained for replay resolution, and how is a retry that arrives after the key has expired treated?
answer_data: Published key retention window and its start reference (observation time of first acceptance)
Receipt expiry instant
Post-expiry treatment rule (treated as a new first occurrence, with the concurrency precondition as the remaining safeguard)
Reference to the retention model that executes receipt disposal

questions.text: Which outcome is recorded when the required idempotency key is absent, malformed or exceeds the declared length or entropy constraints?
answer_data: Outcome code for a missing or malformed key
Problem type identifier for the failure document
Whether any record other than a rejection receipt is appended (none)
Whether the failure is retryable after correction

data_elements.name: Command identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the individual mutation command instance as submitted.

data_elements.name: Idempotency key
data_elements.description: Client-generated value, unique per distinct payload and never reused across differing payloads, used to recognise retries of the same command.

data_elements.name: Command type code
data_elements.description: Governed code naming the mutation command: propose, validate, submit-evidence, approve, reject, activate, supersede, retract or quarantine.

data_elements.name: Canonical request fingerprint
data_elements.description: Digest over the canonical serialisation of the semantically significant command content, used only for comparison; it is never an identifier.

data_elements.name: Command receipt state
data_elements.description: State of the receipt for a composite (client, idempotency key) pair: in-progress, completed, failed or expired.

data_elements.name: Receipt expiry instant
data_elements.description: Instant after which the receipt no longer resolves replays, expressed with seconds and an explicit offset.

artifacts.name: Alias Command Receipt
artifacts.description: Append-only record of one accepted or rejected mutation command: command identifier, composite idempotency lookup key, fingerprint digest, submitting agent reference, command event time, register observation time, outcome code and reference to the records the command produced. Replays return the recorded outcome rather than reprocessing.
media_or_form: structured record in the alias register
interface projection carrying the idempotency key and recorded response
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the register's own receipt identifier; the composite (submitting client reference, idempotency key) is a unique lookup constraint within the retention window, not the identifier. Sequenced per submitting client.

findings.name: Optimistic-concurrency precondition and stale-version detection
findings.description: Every command that targets an existing assertion must supply a validator proving which version the submitter observed. The register compares that validator against the current version token of the target and refuses the command if they differ, so concurrent proposals cannot silently overwrite one another. Precondition failure is semantically distinct from idempotent replay: a replay returns the earlier outcome, a stale validator is a rejection that requires the submitter to re-read and re-derive.

questions.text: Which validator does a mutation command supply to prove it observed the current assertion version, and how is that validator derived?
answer_data: Observed version token of the target assertion
Validator strength (strong validator over the canonical assertion state, or weak validator)
Derivation rule linking the token to the appended record series
Interface projection of the validator, such as an entity-tag carried in a conditional request

questions.text: What distinguishes a stale-version rejection from a duplicate-command replay when both arrive from the same submitting agent?
answer_data: Fingerprint comparison result against the receipt series
Validator comparison result against the current version token
Distinct outcome codes for precondition failure and for replay
Rule that replay resolution is evaluated before precondition evaluation

questions.text: How are two concurrent proposals against the same endpoint pair ordered, and which one is recorded as losing the race?
answer_data: Register-assigned sequence position at durable acceptance
Version token held by each command at submission
Loser outcome code and the recorded reason
Whether the losing submitter must re-propose or may re-target the winning version

questions.text: At what granularity is the concurrency token scoped: the individual assertion, the endpoint pair or the whole alias register?
answer_data: Declared concurrency scope code
Identifier of the scoped unit
Rule for commands that span more than one assertion
Behaviour when a scoped unit has no prior version (creation case)

questions.text: When is a weak validator acceptable for an alias command and when must the validator be strong?
answer_data: Command types requiring a strong validator (activate, supersede, retract, quarantine)
Command types permitted a weak validator (evidence submission that cannot change decided state)
Definition of equivalence used by the weak validator
Outcome code when validator strength is insufficient

data_elements.name: Observed version token
data_elements.description: Validator supplied by the command asserting which version of the target assertion the submitter observed.

data_elements.name: Current version token
data_elements.description: Register-maintained validator for the current version of an assertion, derived from its appended record series.

data_elements.name: Precondition mode
data_elements.description: Whether the command requires the target to match the observed version, to be absent, or to be unmodified since a stated instant.

data_elements.name: Concurrency scope
data_elements.description: The unit over which the version token is defined: assertion, endpoint pair or register partition.

data_elements.name: Conflict outcome code
data_elements.description: Governed code distinguishing precondition failure, in-flight duplicate, key reuse with differing payload and state conflict.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The concurrency precondition is a declared parameter of the command envelope evaluated against the register's current version pointer; it produces no durable object of its own. Its successful outcome is already recorded on the command receipt series and its failure is already recorded in the validation and failure report series. Declaring a third artifact here would create two competing records of the same event and would make the version chain ambiguous, so the precondition is modelled purely as inline envelope data plus a comparison result.

layers.name: Pre-commit Validation Contract
layers.description: The declarative catalogue of checks a command must pass before any assertion record is appended, and the machine-readable outcome record that reports which checks passed, which failed and on which element.

findings.name: Declared validation check set for alias commands
findings.description: A versioned catalogue of named checks with declared severity and applicability per command type. It covers endpoint reference and version presence, the relation-property contract and its vocabulary binding, type/scheme/context compatibility of the two endpoints, required evidence and review sufficiency, contradiction with existing active assertions, violation of declared not-same constraints, effective-interval well-formedness and overlap, and the declared access scope. The catalogue states what must be checked; it does not resolve endpoints, does not infer entailments and does not decide access.

questions.text: Which checks must pass before a proposed alias assertion may be activated, and which are advisory only?
answer_data: Check identifier and its governed name
Severity assigned per command type (blocking or advisory)
Applicability expression naming the command types the check applies to
Catalogue version in force at evaluation time

questions.text: How is the endpoint reference and its version verified without resolving or dereferencing the endpoint itself?
answer_data: Endpoint reference syntax and namespace conformance result
Presence and format of the endpoint version or validator token supplied with the reference
Comparison of the supplied endpoint version against the version last recorded on this assertion
Explicit statement that dereferencing and resolution are delegated to the resolver model

questions.text: Which relation-property, type, scheme and context compatibility rules make a proposed endpoint pairing admissible?
answer_data: Declared relation property and its governed vocabulary term (for example an exact-match or close-match mapping property)
Subject type compatibility rule between the two endpoints
Concept scheme or namespace pairing rule
Context or profile identifier under which the pairing is asserted

questions.text: How are contradictions with existing active assertions and with declared not-same constraints detected and reported?
answer_data: Set of existing active assertions over the same endpoint pair and their relation properties
Disjointness rule violated (for example an exact-match asserted where a broader-match already holds)
Existing distinctness or not-same constraint that the proposal would violate
Contradiction result records with the offending element path, without any attempt to resolve which side is correct

questions.text: How are the effective interval and the declared access scope of a proposal checked against the target assertion?
answer_data: Effective interval start and end with seconds and explicit offset, and the ordering check between them
Overlap result against existing active intervals for the same pair
Declared access scope value and whether it is registered
Result of comparing the declared scope against the scope recorded on the target assertion

data_elements.name: Check identifier
data_elements.description: Governed identifier of a single named check in the catalogue.

data_elements.name: Check severity
data_elements.description: Declared severity of a failed check: blocking violation, warning or informational.

data_elements.name: Check applicability
data_elements.description: The command types and assertion classes to which a check applies.

data_elements.name: Relation-property binding
data_elements.description: Reference to the governed vocabulary term that the assertion's relation property is bound to.

data_elements.name: Not-same constraint reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a recorded distinctness constraint that forbids equating the named endpoints.

data_elements.name: Check catalogue version
data_elements.description: Version of the check catalogue applied to a given command evaluation.

artifacts.name: Alias Command Check Catalogue
artifacts.description: Versioned, non-serial declaration of every named check, its severity, its applicability per command type and the governed vocabulary bindings it enforces. It is the shapes-side counterpart to the per-command validation report and changes only through the register's own registration procedure.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by a governed catalogue IRI in the adopting Dimension's namespace plus an explicit version identifier; individual checks are identified by governed check IRIs that are never reused after retirement.

findings.name: Validation outcome record and machine-readable failure report
findings.description: Each validation run produces one outcome record stating whether the command conforms and, if not, one result per failed check naming the focus element, the path within it, the offending value, the check that produced the result and its severity. The same outcome projects into a machine-readable failure document for the calling interface. The report binds the digest of the exact command payload and catalogue version it judged, so a later edit of either is detectable.

questions.text: What must a validation outcome record contain so a caller can tell exactly which check failed on which element?
answer_data: Overall conformance boolean
Per-result focus element reference and path within it
Offending value and the check identifier that produced the result
Human-readable result message and its language

questions.text: How are check severities mapped to a machine-readable failure response and to an accept, hold or reject outcome?
answer_data: Severity to outcome-code mapping table
Rule that any blocking violation prevents any assertion record being appended
Treatment of warnings (recorded, does not block)
Interface status projection for each outcome code

questions.text: Which evidence of the validated input is bound into the outcome so a later change to the proposal is detectable?
answer_data: Digest of the canonical command payload evaluated
Identifier and version of the proposal version evaluated
Check catalogue version identifier
Register observation time of the evaluation with seconds and explicit offset

questions.text: How are multiple simultaneous check failures reported without collapsing them into a single opaque error?
answer_data: Single problem type identifier for validation failure
Extension array carrying one entry per failed check with its element pointer
Ordering or ranking rule for the primary reported problem
Rule that unrecognised extension members are ignored by consumers

questions.text: Which validation and processing failures are retryable, and how is that signalled to the submitting agent?
answer_data: Retryable classification per outcome code
Whether the same idempotency key may be reused for the retry
Advisory retry delay where the failure is transient
Failures that are permanently non-retryable without a corrected payload

data_elements.name: Conformance flag
data_elements.description: True when the validation run produced no blocking results, false otherwise.

data_elements.name: Validation result entry
data_elements.description: One failed or advisory check with focus element, path, value, source check and severity.

data_elements.name: Problem type identifier
data_elements.description: Stable URI identifying the class of failure reported to the caller.

data_elements.name: Evaluated payload digest
data_elements.description: Digest of the canonical command payload the outcome was computed over.

data_elements.name: Retryability classification
data_elements.description: Whether the outcome is transient and retryable, retryable only after payload correction, or permanent.

artifacts.name: Alias Command Validation Report
artifacts.description: Append-only report for one validation run over one command: conformance flag, ordered result entries with element pointers and severities, the digests of the evaluated payload and catalogue version, and the evaluation observation time. It is the record a decision assertion later cites as the basis it relied on.
media_or_form: problem-details projection for the calling interface
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by a register-assigned report identifier; sequenced per target assertion and per validation attempt so that repeated attempts against the same proposal remain individually citable. Sequence gaps are permitted and never renumbered.

bundles.name: Alias Assertion Lifecycle Commands and Immutable Decision Record
bundles.description: The append-only command sequence that moves an alias assertion through its life: proposal, evidence submission, approval or rejection, activation, supersession, retraction and emergency quarantine, together with the compensating records used when a command applies only partially.
bundles.rationale: Registry practice requires that changes to registered items follow a declared procedure under a named change controller and that entries be marked rather than removed, and provenance practice requires that revision and invalidation be recorded as first-class events attributed to agents. Modelling the commands as an append-only series of immutable records gives a defensible history without duplicating any downstream decision, resolution or enforcement behaviour.

layers.name: Proposal Intake and Evidence Submission
layers.description: How an alias assertion is first proposed, how repeated proposals over the same endpoint pair are versioned, and how supporting evidence is attached to a specific proposal version.

findings.name: Propose command and proposal versioning
findings.description: The propose command records a candidate equivalence: the endpoint references and their versions, the declared relation property and its vocabulary binding, direction and canonical designation, proposed effective interval, declared confidence, asserting authority reference and declared access scope. It creates a new immutable proposal version; it never edits an earlier one. A re-proposal over the same endpoint pair appends a new version linked as a revision of its predecessor.

questions.text: What minimum content must a propose command carry to create the first version of an alias assertion?
answer_data: Two or more endpoint references with their version or validator tokens
Declared relation property and its governed vocabulary binding
Direction and canonical designation, or an explicit statement that the assertion is symmetric
Proposed effective interval, declared confidence and asserting authority reference

questions.text: How is a proposal identified and versioned when the same endpoint pair is proposed repeatedly by different agents?
answer_data: Assertion identifier that is stable across versions
Proposal version identifier and its sequence position
Revision link to the predecessor version
Rule that the endpoint pair is a lookup constraint, not the identifier

questions.text: Which state does a newly recorded proposal enter, and which commands are legal from that state?
answer_data: Initial state code for a recorded proposal
Legal successor commands from that state (validate, submit evidence, approve, reject, retract)
Commands that are illegal from that state (activate before approval, supersede a never-active assertion)
Outcome code for an illegal transition attempt

questions.text: How are the proposing agent and the asserting authority recorded, and how do they differ?
answer_data: Proposing agent reference and its role in the proposal activity
Asserting authority reference on whose behalf the equivalence is claimed
Command event time asserted by the agent and register observation time, recorded separately
Attribution link from the proposal version to the responsible agent

questions.text: What happens to a pending proposal when a competing proposal over the same endpoint pair is recorded before any decision is taken?
answer_data: Whether both proposals remain pending or the earlier is marked overtaken
Version tokens held by each pending proposal
Rule requiring a decision to name the exact proposal version it judges
Outcome code recorded on the proposal that is not carried forward

data_elements.name: Assertion identifier
data_elements.description: Stable identifier of the alias assertion, constant across all its versions.

data_elements.name: Proposal version identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of one immutable proposal version within an assertion's version chain.

data_elements.name: Endpoint reference
data_elements.description: Reference to one identifier endpoint participating in the equivalence, together with its version or validator token.

data_elements.name: Declared confidence
data_elements.description: Confidence declared by the asserting authority, expressed on a scale named by the adopting Dimension.

data_elements.name: Asserting authority reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the party on whose authority the equivalence is claimed; this model records the reference and does not evaluate competence.

data_elements.name: Command event time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the submitting agent asserts the command was issued, with seconds and explicit offset.

artifacts.name: Alias Assertion Proposal Version
artifacts.description: Immutable record of one proposed state of an alias assertion, carrying the endpoint references and versions, relation property binding, direction and canonical designation, proposed effective interval, declared confidence, asserting authority reference, declared access scope, proposing agent and both event and observation times, plus a revision link to its predecessor.
media_or_form: serialised graph projection using mapping and provenance vocabularies
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the assertion identifier plus a monotonic version sequence assigned by the register; the version sequence is never reused or renumbered and gaps are permitted.

findings.name: Evidence submission bound to a proposal version
findings.description: The submit-evidence command appends an evidence item to a named proposal version rather than to the assertion as a whole, so a decision can be traced to exactly the material available when it was taken. Evidence items are immutable: a mistaken attachment is corrected by appending a withdrawal record, never by editing or removing the original entry.

questions.text: How is a submitted evidence item bound to a specific proposal version rather than to the assertion as a whole?
answer_data: Target proposal version identifier
Evidence item identifier and its sequence position within the version
Digest of the evidence payload or of its external reference
Evidence role code stating which check it is offered to satisfy

questions.text: Which provenance attributes must accompany an evidence item for it to count toward the required-evidence check?
answer_data: Submitting agent reference and the party responsible for the evidence content
Source system or document reference from which the evidence was obtained
Evidence generation time and register observation time, recorded separately
Method or verification procedure by which the evidence was produced

questions.text: Can an evidence item be withdrawn, and what record remains if the underlying material must be removed?
answer_data: Withdrawal record referencing the withdrawn evidence item and its reason code
Rule that the original entry and its digest are retained as a tombstone
Reference to the retention or privacy model that executes any removal of the payload itself
Effect of withdrawal on any decision that already cited the item (none retroactively; a new decision is required)

questions.text: How is restricted or confidential evidence declared so the decision record stays readable when the evidence itself is not?
answer_data: Declared access scope or classification code on the evidence item
Which fields remain visible when the payload is withheld (identifier, digest, role, provenance summary)
Reference to the authorization model that decides who may read the payload
Outcome code when a reader requests a withheld payload

questions.text: Which command corrects an evidence item that was attached to the wrong proposal version?
answer_data: Withdrawal record on the incorrect binding
New evidence submission against the correct proposal version
Idempotency key and concurrency validator required for both commands
Link recording that the second submission compensates the first

data_elements.name: Evidence item identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of one immutable evidence attachment.

data_elements.name: Evidence role code
data_elements.description: Which validation check or review requirement the evidence item is offered to satisfy.

data_elements.name: Evidence payload digest
data_elements.description: Digest over the evidence payload or over the canonical form of its external reference.

data_elements.name: Evidence access classification
data_elements.description: Declared classification or access scope governing visibility of the evidence payload.

data_elements.name: Evidence observation time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the register durably recorded the evidence item, with seconds and explicit offset.

artifacts.name: Evidence Attachment Record
artifacts.description: Immutable record binding one evidence item to one proposal version, carrying the evidence role, payload digest or external reference, provenance attributes, declared classification, submitting agent and both generation and observation times. Withdrawals are appended as separate records in the same series.
media_or_form: external document or dataset reference with digest
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by a register-assigned evidence identifier; sequenced per proposal version. Where the evidence originates in a master system, that system's identifier is recorded as the authoritative source reference alongside the register identifier.

layers.name: Immutable Decision Record
layers.description: How approval and rejection are recorded as immutable decision assertions bound to the exact proposal version and validation report they relied on, referencing but never evaluating the deciding authority.

findings.name: Approve and reject decision assertions
findings.description: An approve or reject command appends a decision assertion naming the decided proposal version, the validation report relied on, the deciding authority reference, the decision outcome and reason code, and both decision event time and register observation time. Decision assertions are immutable; a reversal is expressed by appending a later decision or a retraction, never by editing the earlier record. The register records that a decision was made by a named authority; it does not determine whether that authority was competent to make it.

questions.text: What does an approve or reject decision assertion record, and what does it deliberately not record?
answer_data: Decision outcome code and governed reason code
Decided proposal version identifier and validation report identifier
Deciding authority reference and decision event time
Explicit exclusion: no authorization evaluation result and no enforcement instruction

questions.text: How is the deciding authority referenced without this model determining whether that authority was competent to decide?

Delegation or mandate reference presented with the decision

Outcome code when the authority reference is absent or unresolvable in form

Reversal expressed as a later decision assertion or a retraction record
Link type relating the reversing record to the reversed one
Effect on the assertion's current state pointer

Mandate or break-glass reference supporting the basis

Whether advisory check warnings were overridden and on what recorded ground

layers.name: Activation, Supersession, Retraction and Quarantine
layers.description: The commands that change which assertion is in force: activation with an effective interval, supersession of a conflicting or outdated assertion, retraction of one previously in force, emergency quarantine marking, and the compensating records used after a partial failure.

findings.name: Activation and supersession with effective intervals
findings.description: Activation makes an approved assertion version the one in force from a stated effective start, optionally until a stated end. Supersession appends a record relating a new version to the one it replaces and closes the predecessor's effective interval; the predecessor is retained and remains readable. Where two active assertions over the same endpoint pair would conflict, the register records the conflict and the supersession that resolves it, and does not attempt to decide the truth of either.

questions.text: Which event marks an assertion as active, and what is recorded at that moment?

Approved proposal version being activated and the decision assertion authorising it
Effective start instant and optional effective end, each with seconds and explicit offset
Register observation time of the activation, recorded separately from the effective start

questions.text: How is the effective interval of an activation set, and what happens when it overlaps an existing active interval for the same endpoint pair?

Overlap detection result against existing active intervals
Whether overlap is permitted for compatible relation properties and forbidden for conflicting ones
Outcome code and required supersession when overlap is not permitted

Recorded precedence rule applied, including authority precedence where declared

Reference to the decision assertion authorising the supersession

Terminal state code applied to the superseded version
Closed effective interval on the superseded version
Rule that the superseded record remains readable and citable

Reference to the resolver model that owns any redirect or merge behaviour

findings.name: Retraction, emergency quarantine and compensating records
findings.description: Retraction records that an assertion previously in force is withdrawn by its asserting or deciding authority, closing its effective interval and marking it invalidated without removing it. Emergency quarantine marks an assertion as not to be relied upon pending review, and may be applied before or after a decision. When a command applies only partially, the register derives a compensating record set that restores a consistent state by appending counter-records; it never rewrites or deletes what was already appended.

questions.text: What exactly does a retract command assert about an assertion that was previously in force?

Whether the assertion is withdrawn from a stated instant or treated as never valid
Invalidating agent and invalidation time

Required review deadline or expiry of the hold
Reference to the party permitted to append a lift record and the required decision basis

Outcome code recorded when compensation itself cannot complete and manual custodial action is required

Retention class and any legal-hold reference
Reference to the retention model that owns schedule and erasure execution
Reference to the privacy model where personal-data erasure duties apply

artifacts.name: Alias Retraction and Quarantine Record
artifacts.description: Immutable record of a retraction or quarantine marking: terminal state applied, reason and basis codes, requesting and invalidating agent references, invalidation time and register observation time, any review deadline, and the tombstone marker preserving identifier and version chain.
media_or_form: provenance graph projection using invalidation relations
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by a register-assigned record identifier; sequenced per assertion within the same terminal-state series so retraction, quarantine and lift records are ordered without renumbering.

artifacts.name: Compensating Record Plan
artifacts.description: Derived, recorded plan listing each record already appended by a partially applied command and the counter-record proposed to neutralise it, with the originating command identifier, the failure outcome code and the concurrency validators required to apply each counter-record. It is a calculation and a record, not an execution.

Canonical request fingerprint digest

All time values in the payload carry seconds and an explicit offset

Reference to the previously recorded outcome when the classification is a completed replay
Outcome code when the classification is a conflict

The receipt series for the composite key is readable
