composition.purpose: WM-XCT-036 is registered as a child of WM-XCT-011 and inherits the subject and identifier definitions it governs. This model contributes only equivalence assertions over those identifiers and the mutation-command surface that changes them; identifier minting, subject typing and register-wide governance remain with the parent.

composition.target: Host entity, catalogue or registry model that carries the aliased endpoints
composition.purpose: Attach the alias assertion and its command surface to a host subject record without altering the host's own identity or lifecycle, in the same way an also-known-as set attaches to a subject document and a mapping property attaches to a concept.

Carry the declared access scope, the actor reference and the deciding authority reference on the command envelope and the decision record. Evaluating whether an actor may issue a command, and enforcing that evaluation, belong entirely to the target.

Emit the correlation identifier, command identifier, idempotency key, fingerprint digest, actor reference and outcome code for every accepted, rejected and replayed command. Audit-record construction, tamper-evidence, retention and query are owned by the target; this model neither writes nor reads audit records.

composition.target: W3C SKOS mapping properties (skos:exactMatch, skos:closeMatch, skos:relatedMatch, skos:broadMatch, skos:narrowMatch)
composition.purpose: Bind the declared relation property of an alias assertion to a governed external vocabulary term, and take the vocabulary's disjointness statements as the basis for the contradiction check. SKOS defines no mutation commands, so nothing of this model's command lifecycle is derived from it and no conformance is claimed.

composition.target: OWL 2 individual equality and difference (owl:sameAs, owl:differentFrom)
composition.purpose: Bind strong equivalence and explicit distinctness assertions to a governed logical vocabulary and take the absence of a unique name assumption as the reason distinctness must be asserted rather than inferred. Entailment and consistency checking are performed by an external reasoner, not here.

composition.target: Interface projection model for the alias register (HTTP or MCP binding)
composition.purpose: Bind the model-level idempotency key and concurrency validator to concrete transport constructs and map outcome codes to transport status codes and failure documents. Transport execution, connection handling and retry scheduling are owned by the target.

composition.target: Adopting-Dimension retention, disposition and privacy model
composition.purpose: Carry the retention-class reference, legal-hold reference and disposition-decision reference on terminal-state and evidence records. Retention scheduling, erasure execution and personal-data rectification duties are owned by the target; this model only appends tombstones and disposition references.

composition.target: Status, revocation or resolution service for aliased endpoints
composition.purpose: Expose the assertion's current lifecycle state and effective interval for consumption by resolvers and status checkers. Status checking, resolution, canonical redirect execution and endpoint merge are defined and performed by the target, consistent with credential status semantics being defined outside the data model that carries the status reference.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names one Alias Register Custodian who is the recorded change controller for the alias register, its command vocabulary and its check catalogue, and publishes how that role is reassigned when the holder is unavailable.

The Dimension publishes the registration procedure for alias assertions: what a propose command must contain, which checks are blocking, what evidence and review each relation property requires, and which authority may decide.
The Dimension publishes the idempotency-key retention window, the canonicalisation profile and digest algorithm used for fingerprints, and the concurrency scope at which version tokens are defined.
The Dimension declares the confidence scale in use and the precedence rule applied when two authorities assert conflicting equivalences, since neither is fixed by this model.
The Dimension binds each referenced model — authority, audit, retention, notification and resolution — to a concrete owner package before any command surface is exposed.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Command type codes, check identifiers, outcome codes, reason codes and problem type URIs are minted in a governed namespace owned by the adopting Dimension and are never reused after retirement. Relation properties are referenced by their external vocabulary IRI and are not re-minted locally. Assertion, proposal-version, evidence, decision and transition identifiers are minted in the register's own namespace; endpoint references retain the namespace of their owning master system. Problem type URIs are stable across versions because consumers key behaviour on them.
registry_links: The Vercy registry record vr.wm-xct-036 is the authoritative registration entry for this model, its status and its review state.
The parent registration WM-XCT-011 governs the identifier and subject definitions this model asserts equivalence over.
The external relation-property vocabulary registries supplying mapping and equality terms are referenced by IRI and versioned independently of this model.
The adopting Dimension's problem type registry and check catalogue registry are named in AGENTS.md and are versioned alongside the command vocabulary.

canonicalization_rules: Serialise only semantically significant command content: command type, target assertion reference, endpoint references and their version tokens, relation-property binding, direction and canonical designation, effective interval, declared confidence, declared access scope and evidence references. Exclude transport headers, trace identifiers, retry counters and the register observation time.

Order object members lexicographically by key and order unordered sets of endpoint references by their canonical reference string, so that a symmetric assertion produces one fingerprint regardless of submission order.

Normalise all time values to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset before digesting; preserve the submitted offset rather than converting to UTC, and use -00:00 only where the local offset is genuinely unknown.
Normalise identifier references to their governed canonical form (case, percent-encoding and trailing-separator rules) without dereferencing them.
Record the canonicalisation profile identifier and digest algorithm identifier alongside every fingerprint so a stored fingerprint remains interpretable after the profile changes.
patch_rules: The record series are append-only. There is no in-place patch of a proposal version, evidence item, validation report, decision assertion or transition record.

A change to an assertion is expressed as a new proposal version linked as a revision of its predecessor; a change to a decision is expressed as a later decision assertion or a retraction record; a change to evidence is expressed as a withdrawal record plus a new attachment.
Every command that changes state must carry an idempotency key and a concurrency validator, and must be safe to replay: a replay returns the recorded outcome and appends nothing further.

Partial application is repaired by appending counter-records derived from a recorded compensation plan, each applied by its own command with its own key and validator; records are never rewritten or removed to repair state.

Only the register-maintained derived pointers — current version token, current lifecycle state, effective-interval index — change without a new appended record, and they are always recomputable from the record series.
compatibility_rules: Adding a new advisory check, a new optional command field or a new reason code is a minor change; existing commands remain valid.

Raising a check from advisory to blocking, removing or renaming a check identifier, changing a relation-property binding, narrowing an accepted value set or shortening the idempotency-key retention window is a breaking change requiring a new catalogue major version and a published transition period.
Problem type URIs, outcome codes and reason codes are stable identifiers; a change of meaning requires a new code rather than redefinition of an existing one.
Consumers must ignore unrecognised extension members in failure documents and unrecognised advisory result entries, so that additive changes do not break existing integrations.
Every record states the check catalogue version and command vocabulary version under which it was produced, so historic records remain interpretable after a breaking change.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: the identifier assigned by the system of record that governs the artifact — the registration authority's item identifier for a register entry, or the deciding authority's case or decision identifier for a decision assertion. Where such an identifier exists it is the identity of record.

Governed global identifier or IRI: a resolvable identifier in a governed namespace, such as the register's own assertion IRI or an external identifier IRI, used when no master-system identifier exists.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, recorded together with the minting agent reference and the minting instant, used only when neither of the above is available.

Never an identifier: a date or timestamp, a sequence position, an endpoint pair, an idempotency key or a canonical request fingerprint. The idempotency key is a scoped uniqueness constraint within its retention window and the fingerprint is a comparison value only.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are RFC 3339 date-time strings that include seconds and an explicit offset of Z or +/-hh:mm; -00:00 is used only where the instant is known in UTC but the local offset is genuinely unknown. Command event time (the instant the submitting agent asserts the command was issued) is recorded separately from register observation or ingestion time (the instant the register durably recorded it), and both are recorded separately from the effective interval start and end that state when the assertion is in force. Decision event time and invalidation time are likewise distinct from observation time. These values must never be collapsed into a single field, and any ordering or expiry rule states which of them it uses.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named as `<assertion identifier>/<artifact kind>/<zero-padded monotonic sequence>`, with command receipts sequenced per submitting client and all other series sequenced per assertion and per kind. Sequence positions are assigned at durable acceptance, are never reused and are never renumbered; gaps arising from rejected or abandoned commands are permitted and must be left in place, since closing a gap would falsify the version chain.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every serial artifact carries a content digest over its canonical serialisation together with the digest of its predecessor in the same series, so any later alteration of an earlier record is detectable within the register itself. Validation reports additionally bind the digest of the exact command payload and the check catalogue version they evaluated, and decision assertions additionally bind the digests of the proposal version and validation report they relied on. Where a record is cryptographically secured, the securing mechanism is named on the record; the integrity guarantee here is internal to the record series and does not depend on, and does not substitute for, the referenced audit-trail model.

policies: Immutability: prior assertions, evidence items, validation reports, decision assertions and transition records are never edited or deleted. Every change appends a new version, a counter-record or a later decision, and the superseded record remains readable and citable.

Safe retry: every mutation command carries an idempotency key and an optimistic-concurrency validator. A replay returns the recorded outcome and applies nothing further; a stale validator is rejected and must be re-derived from a fresh read. These two mechanisms are evaluated in that order and their failures are reported with distinct outcome codes.

No inference and no resolution: the register records asserted equivalences and validation outcomes only. It never computes candidate matches, never materialises transitive or substitution closure, never dereferences or merges endpoints, and never issues a redirect.

Reference, do not assume, authority: the register validates that an authority reference and a declared access scope are present, registered and no broader than the target's recorded scope. Whether the actor may act is decided by the referenced authorization model, and enforcement of that decision happens there.

Validate before append: no assertion record is appended while any blocking check fails. Advisory failures are recorded on the validation report and may be overridden only by a decision assertion that names the overridden checks and its decision basis.

Retain rather than remove: terminal states are expressed by marking and tombstoning, following registry practice that entries are marked deprecated or obsolete and retained for historic purposes; physical removal is requested from the retention model and never performed here.

read: Reads are safe and side-effect free: reading an assertion, a version chain, a validation report or a decision never changes state and never advances an idempotency receipt.
A read returns the current lifecycle state, the effective interval and the current version token, so a caller can immediately derive the concurrency validator for a following mutation.

Superseded, retracted and quarantined records remain readable by identifier and version; default result sets exclude terminal states, and an explicit parameter includes them so nothing is silently missing.

Reads of records with a restricted declared classification return the record's identifier, state and digests while withholding the classified payload, and the authorization model decides who may see the payload.
create: Every create command carries an idempotency key, a canonical request fingerprint and, where a target already exists, a concurrency validator; a create without a key is rejected before any evaluation.
Creation proceeds only after replay classification returns first occurrence, the precondition holds and the validation run reports no blocking violation.
A successful create appends exactly one immutable record plus its command receipt, and advances only derived pointers.
A concurrent duplicate arriving while the original is still processing is reported as a conflict rather than being processed twice; a completed replay returns the recorded outcome unchanged.
update: There is no in-place update of any appended record. An update is an append of a new proposal version, a later decision assertion, a transition record or a withdrawal record.
Every update command must supply the version validator it observed; a mismatch is a precondition failure and nothing is appended.
Only register-maintained derived pointers change without an appended record, and every one of them is recomputable from the record series alone.
Corrections to evidence or to a mis-targeted command are recorded as compensating appends that link explicitly to the records they neutralise.
delete: This model performs no physical deletion. Withdrawal of an assertion is a retract command that appends a terminal-state record, closes the effective interval and preserves the assertion identifier, its full version chain, the reason code and all record digests as a tombstone.
Quarantine is a reversible marking that suppresses reliance without removing anything; lifting a quarantine is itself an appended record.
Superseded, rejected and retracted records are retained for historic reference, consistent with registry practice that entries are marked rather than removed, and remain resolvable by identifier.

Retention duration, disposition scheduling, legal hold and any physical erasure or crypto-shredding of record payloads are executed by the adopting Dimension's retention and disposition model; where personal data is involved, erasure and rectification duties are executed by the referenced privacy model. This model records only the retention-class reference, the disposition-decision reference and the resulting tombstone, and never initiates or performs the erasure itself.

Deletion of the register as a whole, or closure of it to new registrations, is a governance act of the Alias Register Custodian recorded as a register-level status change; existing records remain readable after closure.

roles.name: Alias Register Custodian
responsibilities: Act as the recorded change controller for the alias register, its command vocabulary, its check catalogue and its problem type registry.
Publish and version the registration procedure, the idempotency-key retention window and the canonicalisation profile.
Approve breaking changes to the check catalogue and manage the published transition period.
Record register-level status changes such as closure to new registrations.

roles.name: Proposing Agent
responsibilities: Submit propose, submit-evidence and correction commands with a well-formed idempotency key and a freshly derived concurrency validator.
Supply endpoint references with version tokens, the declared relation property, the proposed effective interval, the declared confidence and the asserting authority reference.
Re-read and re-derive after a precondition failure rather than retrying with a stale validator.
Retry safely using the same key after a transient failure and never reuse a key with a changed payload.

roles.name: Reviewing Authority
responsibilities: Take approve and reject decisions and have them recorded against the exact proposal version and validation report relied on.
State the decision basis and, where advisory checks are overridden, name the overridden checks and the ground for the override.
Express reversals as later decisions or retractions rather than requesting edits to earlier records.
Authorise activations and supersessions and record the precedence rule applied when active assertions conflict.

roles.name: Evidence Steward
responsibilities: Ensure evidence items carry their role, digest, source reference, generation time and responsible party before submission.
Declare the classification of restricted evidence so decisions remain readable when payloads are withheld.
Append withdrawal records for evidence attached in error and coordinate any payload removal with the retention and privacy models.
Confirm that the required-evidence check is satisfied by material bound to the version actually under decision.

roles.name: Platform Integrator
responsibilities: Bind model-level idempotency keys and concurrency validators to the concrete interface projection and map outcome codes to transport statuses and failure documents.
Implement the receipt store and its published expiry policy, and ensure composite lookup keys include the client identity.
Forward correlation records to the referenced audit model and lifecycle signals to the referenced notification and resolution models without adding local audit or delivery semantics.
Recompute derived pointers deterministically from the record series after any restore or replication event.

access.default_rule: Deny by default at every scope. A command is considered only if its envelope declares an access scope that is registered and is no broader than the scope recorded on the target assertion; validation reports the presence, registration and breadth of that declaration. The access decision itself — whether the named actor may issue this command against this target — is made by the referenced authorization model, and this model records the decision reference without re-deriving or enforcing it.
exceptions: Emergency quarantine may be requested under a break-glass mandate before a decision exists; the mandate reference and quarantine basis are recorded, and the hold carries a review deadline after which it must be confirmed or lifted by an appended record.

Evidence attachments may carry a restricted classification: the decision assertion, its reason code and the evidence identifier and digest stay readable at the finding scope while the payload is withheld at the artifact scope.

A proposal may be embargoed so that its existence and state are readable but its endpoint references are withheld until activation, for cases where disclosing a proposed equivalence would itself be sensitive.
Custodians retain read access to terminal-state and tombstone records regardless of the assertion's declared scope, so that history remains auditable after withdrawal.
Where an assertion links identifiers of natural persons, the referenced privacy model may narrow the readable scope below the declared scope; the narrower of the two always governs.
audit_requirements: Every accepted, rejected and replayed command emits a correlation record containing the command identifier, idempotency key, fingerprint digest, submitting agent reference, target assertion and version, outcome code, decision reference where one exists, command event time and register observation time.
Every break-glass quarantine, every override of an advisory check and every access-scope exception emits a correlation record naming the mandate or override ground.

Correlation records are handed to the referenced audit-trail model, which owns their storage, ordering guarantees, tamper-evidence, retention and query; this model neither stores nor interprets audit records and its own integrity guarantee does not depend on them.
The register's internal record digests and predecessor chaining are maintained independently so that internal tampering is detectable even if the external audit trail is unavailable.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md first and resolve Name, Type and Registry ID to confirm which model and which register instance is being addressed.
Read the Specification URL to obtain the model boundary, the command vocabulary, the check catalogue version in force and the identity and timestamp rules before issuing any command.
Read the Storage type URL to learn how the append-only record series are projected into the concrete store, including how derived pointers are recomputed and how sequence positions are assigned.
Read the Interface URL to learn how the idempotency key, the concurrency validator and the outcome codes are bound to the concrete transport, and where the problem type registry is published.
Read the Processes URL last to learn the registration procedure, the evidence and review requirements per relation property, the decision authorities and the compensation and quarantine procedures.

Resolve the referenced authorization, audit, retention and resolution models named in AGENTS.md before issuing any mutation command, since this model records references into them but performs none of their functions.

coverage.claim: This is a defensible, standards-grounded structure for WM-XCT-036 Alias / Same-as Mapping: it defines the equivalence assertion together with its complete append-only mutation-command surface, grounded in HTTP conditional-request and idempotency semantics, problem-details failure reporting, shapes-based validation reporting, provenance revision and invalidation patterns, registry change-control and status-marking practice, and the mapping and equality vocabularies whose disjointness statements make contradiction checking possible. It is not a claim of conformance to any of those standards, and it deliberately owns no matching, inference, resolution, authorization, audit or deletion behaviour.

checklist.notes: Identity priority runs master-system identifier, then governed IRI, then minted UUID or ULID. Assertion identifiers are stable across versions; proposal, evidence, decision and transition records are separately identified and sequenced. Idempotency keys and fingerprints are explicitly excluded from being identifiers.

Propose, validate, submit evidence, approve or reject, activate, supersede, retract and quarantine are defined with states, legal transitions, preconditions and terminal markings; every transition is an appended immutable record.

Endpoint pairing, direction and canonical designation, relation-property binding, supersession links, revision links, compensation links and not-same constraints are modelled. Entailment over those relationships is explicitly external.

Command event time, decision event time, invalidation time, register observation time and effective interval start and end are distinct fields, all RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset. Overlap and ordering checks are part of the check set.

Proposing agent, asserting authority, deciding authority, evidence source and invalidating agent are recorded; records carry revision and derivation links and predecessor digests following the provenance revision and invalidation pattern.

Change control sits with the named Alias Register Custodian; endpoint references retain their owning master system's namespace; downstream delivery, resolution, authorization, audit and retention ownership are assigned to referenced models.

A versioned check catalogue with declared severity and applicability, and a per-run outcome report with focus element, path, value, source check and severity, plus a machine-readable failure projection with one entry per failed check.

Deny by default; the declared access scope is validated for registration and breadth but never decided here. Exceptions cover break-glass quarantine, restricted evidence, embargoed proposals, custodial history access and privacy narrowing.

No physical deletion. Retraction appends a terminal-state record and tombstone preserving identifier, version chain, reason and digests; retention class, legal hold and erasure execution are delegated to the retention and privacy models, with only the disposition reference recorded here.

Relation properties bind to external vocabulary IRIs rather than local re-minting; failure reporting uses a stable problem type with an ignorable extension array; validators and idempotency keys have declared transport bindings; the model is projection-independent.

Every mutation requires a key and a validator, evaluated in that order, with distinct outcome codes for replay, in-flight duplicate, key reuse with differing payload and stale version. Receipt expiry and post-expiry behaviour are specified.

Failure classification, retryability signalling, partial-failure detection and a derived compensating-record plan are defined; compensation is appended and applied by separate keyed commands, never executed as a rewrite.

Alias assertions relate identifier endpoints, not locations. Where an aliased subject is itself spatial, that geometry belongs to the host subject model, not to the equivalence assertion or its command surface.

Declared confidence is carried as an opaque value on the proposal, but no confidence scale, no comparability rule between scales and no precedence arithmetic for competing authorities is fixed by any primary source consulted. The adopting Dimension must declare its scale; this node is a gap, not canonical structure.

known_omissions: No cross-register distributed transaction protocol. Compensation is defined within a single alias register; a command spanning two registers is out of scope and no two-phase commit or saga coordination is specified.
No canonical confidence scale, no rule for comparing confidence values expressed on different scales, and no arithmetic for combining evidence into a confidence value.
No bulk or batch command semantics beyond per-command idempotency: batch atomicity, partial batch acceptance and batch-level validators are not specified.
The securing mechanism for decision assertions is referenced as an option but no signature suite, key management or proof format is selected.
Machine-readable shapes for the check catalogue are referenced by identifier; the concrete shapes graph and its authoring rules belong to the adopting Dimension.

Reciprocity handling is only partially specified: the practice of not treating an alias as equivalence unless the reverse assertion exists is recorded as a check, but no procedure is defined for soliciting or verifying the reciprocal assertion from the other endpoint's owner.

No normative status enumeration is adopted from ISO/IEC 11179-6, since only its catalogue record was accessible; the lifecycle state codes here are model-specific and are not claimed to align with that standard's registration statuses.
conflicts: RFC 9457 recommends representing the single most relevant problem and discourages generic batch problem types, while the validation contract must report every failed check at once. This model resolves the tension by emitting one stable validation-failure problem type with an errors extension array carrying per-check pointers, following the specification's own validation-error example pattern. This is a documented accommodation, not a conformance claim.

The Idempotency-Key HTTP Header Field specification is an expired IETF Internet-Draft (draft-07, 2025-10-15), not a standard. Its status choices for an in-flight duplicate and for key reuse with a differing payload are widely implemented but not normative, whereas RFC 9110 normatively assigns 412 to a failed precondition. Implementations therefore differ on whether a reused key with a changed payload is a 409 or a 422, and this model keeps its own outcome codes primary with transport mapping declared by the interface projection.

SKOS makes exactMatch symmetric and transitive and asserts disjointness with broadMatch and relatedMatch, while OWL sameAs carries full substitution semantics under no unique name assumption. The two are not interchangeable: recording an assertion bound to a SKOS mapping property does not license OWL-strength substitution, and this model computes neither closure. A consumer that treats them as equivalent will over-infer.

DID Core advises that alias assertions should not be treated as equivalence unless reciprocated, whereas a great deal of federated practice treats a single-direction same-as assertion as sufficient. This model records direction and reciprocity explicitly and makes reciprocity a declared check rather than an assumption, which is stricter than common practice.

Registry practice retains entries permanently for historic purposes, while privacy regimes may compel erasure of records containing personal data. The model resolves this by separating the tombstone, which is always retained here, from the payload, whose erasure is executed by the referenced retention and privacy models — but the two obligations remain in genuine tension and the adopting Dimension must decide the boundary.
regional_assumptions: Time values follow RFC 3339 with explicit offsets; no jurisdiction-specific business calendar, working-day arithmetic or local civil-time interpretation is assumed for effective intervals, and any such interpretation must be declared by the adopting Dimension.

Where alias assertions link identifiers of natural persons, jurisdictions with rectification and erasure duties (for example EU or UK data-protection regimes) may require the referenced privacy model to erase evidence payloads while this model retains only the tombstone; jurisdictions without such duties may retain complete history including payloads.

Legal hold, records-retention schedules and the admissibility requirements for decision records are jurisdiction-specific and are owned by the adopting Dimension; this model carries only the references.
Authority precedence between competing asserting authorities is assumed to be declared locally; no cross-border or cross-sector precedence order is asserted here.
No assumption is made that the register and its referenced authorization, audit and retention models are operated in the same jurisdiction or under the same data-residency constraints.
adversarial_checks: Does any function perform matching, inference, resolution, merge, authorization, audit-log writing, notification delivery or physical deletion? Checked against all ten functions: each is confined to canonicalisation and digesting, receipt classification, validator comparison, check evaluation, failure-document composition, record appending or compensation-plan derivation. Every function that touches an external concern emits a reference or correlation identifier and explicitly disclaims the target's behaviour.

Could the idempotency key or the request fingerprint be mistaken for an identifier? Explicitly forbidden in the identity priority rule: the key is a scoped uniqueness constraint within its retention window and the fingerprint is a comparison value. Record identity always comes from the master-system identifier, the governed IRI or a minted UUID or ULID.

Does replay resolution mask a genuine lost update? Ordering is specified: replay classification runs before precondition evaluation, and the two produce distinct outcome codes, so a stale validator can never be silently absorbed as a duplicate. Receipt expiry is published and post-expiry retries fall back to the concurrency validator as the remaining safeguard.

Does the model quietly own audit semantics by keeping receipts and transition records? Receipts, reports, decisions and transitions are domain state of the register with internal digest chaining for tamper-detection; the audit-trail model owns audit-record storage, tamper-evidence, retention and query. The internal integrity guarantee is stated as independent of, and not a substitute for, that model.

Does declaring an access scope amount to making an access decision? No. Validation confirms only that the declared scope is present, registered and not broader than the scope recorded on the target. Whether the actor may act is decided by the referenced authorization model, whose decision reference is recorded rather than re-derived.

Does the model claim conformance to any cited standard? No. SKOS and OWL bindings are declared as alignments; the ISO registration standard is used only as evidence that a governed registration procedure exists, because only its catalogue record was accessible; the idempotency-key draft is cited as expired work in progress; and the accommodation of the problem-details single-problem guidance is recorded as a conflict rather than presented as conformance.

Is any structural node unsupported by a primary source? Every bundle, layer, finding, function and composition link cites at least one primary source from IETF, W3C or ISO/IEC. The one node without primary support — a normative confidence scale — is recorded as a gap in the checklist and as a known omission rather than being modelled as canonical structure.
